source.version_note: Final Sensors 21(8):2646article, published9April2021.2646is the article identifier, not a year or participant count. Both authors share contribution credit.
source.verification_method: All thirteen supplied pages, three figures, seven tables and all 45 references read. Item-group table, avatar images, procedure diagram and multi-axis graph visually inspected. Crossref/publisher verify identity/date. The cited Gray2007one-page article and figure were read in full for scale/target verification; its external methods supplement was not read. Statistical checks reconstruct published summaries only.

citation.title: Who Is to Blame? The Appearance of Virtual Agents and the Attribution of Perceived Responsibility

reading.source_scope_note: A Japanese web study compares five virtual-agent presentations during a sound-guessing task programmed to fail, with 61 pre-survey respondents and 319 main participations. Outcomes are trustworthiness ratings and perceived responsibility or cause, not real agent fault. Assignment is not documented as random. Published agency and experience item groups are mixed, and correlations use five group means. No stronger effect of experience or measured guilt is established.
access_limits: All thirteen supplied pages, all figures/tables and complete45-entry bibliography read. No Supplementary, DataAvailability or Correction section was located on the inspected publisher page. This is a bounded access observation, not proof that no other materials or later correction exist. No raw data, analysis syntax, item-level scores, complete survey flow or preregistration was retrieved.

The source’s pre-survey questionnaire and main questionnaire are inTables1and3; introductory speech inTable4. Actual administered item ordering/grouping and exact analysis cannot be verified from displayed tables alone.

Cited primary Gray/Gray/Wegner2007 Dimensions of Mind Perception, DOI10.1126/science.1134475, was read from its author’s public two-pagePDF:cover plus the complete one-page article and figure.148139bytes, SHA256c19a371783e9c76a335f198f4efa69bf494e98ed3ef2c1e88ec896e472f20156. SourceURL:https://dtg.sites.fas.harvard.edu/DANWEGNER/pub/Gray%2C%20Gray%2C%20%26%20Wegner%20%282007%29.pdf . Its separate supporting methods/TableS1were not read; no additional queued corpus item or replication credit is claimed.

Other cited studies, books and the2011Grayarticle were not separately fully read. A targeted search for Shaver1970confirmed the named defensive-attribution source but did not provide a sufficiently verified original definition/full text; do not turn the current paper’s broad shorthand into a new canonical definition.

No individual data, author contact, private files, author-code execution, full-paper Markdown archive or clinical/legal intervention. Original task deception and debriefing are source methods, not instructions to deceive current users.

study.pre_survey: 61Japanese YahooCrowdSourcing participants,49male/10female/2undisclosed, age25–49, mean39.6, paid60yen. Brief2–3second introduction clips and six capacity items. Per-target allocation/repeated rating structure, item-level reliability and exact administered grouping are not fully described; no forced2×2capacity intervention.
study.main_sample: Main groupNs60noappearance,59human,69robot,59dog,72angel, total319, paid80yen. Adults roughly20–49, with unequal gender proportions. The source attributes unequalNs to applicants for separate online tasks; random assignment and unique identity across tasks/pilot are not documented. SimilarNsor another study’s null gender effect do not remove confounding.
study.stimuli: Human-like, robot-like, dog-like, angel-like avatars plus voice/subtitles with no visual appearance. All voices use the same named synthesis system. One image per type bundles morphology, species/fantasy identity, style and gender cues; angel is not an independently validated substitute for God.
study.task: Three sound-choice trials with supposed joint success requiring both user and agent correct. Outcomes are programmed to end in failure regardless of participant answers. Thus no user-versus-agent actual error is identified. Participants are debriefed and can withdraw their data; withdrawal counts are not reported.
study.measures: Trustworthiness before/after task on1–7; self/agent responsibility on independent0–100ratings explicitly not required to sum100. Q5asks who erred; methods say seven-point response butTable7is binary and totals318, with angel71versus72recruited. Mapping/missingness unknown. These are perceived responsibility and cause, not actual culpability.
study.construct_problem: Table1defines agency asQ1fear, Q2self-control, Q3pleasure and experience asQ4memory, Q5hunger, Q6morality. These mix the cited dimensions. Under the cited framework, the intended agency items areQ2/Q4/Q6and experienceQ1/Q3/Q5; this is not repaired by simply swapping whole labels. Raw item data/fielded form are needed before recalculating scores.
study.descriptive_results: Table5post-trust dog4.93versusrobot4.13and self-responsibility angel53.19versusrobot37.46. Agent-responsibility omnibus not significant. Trust before failure varies4.18–4.55and no group difference detected. These observations do not demonstrate that pre/post change differs by condition or that humanlike design produces warranted trust.
study.critical_F: Every reported omnibus F4,314=2.4004matches the95th-percentile critical value, despite different pvalues. Pairwise3.9163and3.9092similarly match criticalF1,126andF1,139. This is a reporting error substituting cutoffs for observed statistics. It does not by itself invalidate the pvalue conclusions.
study.summary_reconstruction: Using rounded means/SDsand statedNs:preF≈1.093, p≈.360; postF≈2.873, p≈.0232; selfF≈2.505, p≈.0422; agentF≈1.445, p≈.219. Dog/robotpost pairF≈12.259, p≈.000641andangel/robotselfF≈10.142, p≈.001789; even multiplying by10pairwise tests gives≈.00641/.01789. These support the reported major contrast directions while not verifying exact raw output or the original adjustment implementation.
study.correlations: Table6coefficients reproduce correlations of five avatar-condition means, not319independent person-level observations. Examples agency/postr≈.727, p≈.164andexperience/postr≈−.588, p≈.297, n5. The pre-survey and main sample are separate; aggregation prevents individual mediation or a causal superiority claim for experience.
study.binary_result: Table7counts reconstructχ²4=8.5033, p≈.07479, n318. This does not cross.05and is not proof of an appearance effect on categorical fault choice. Residual procedure/adjustment is insufficiently specified. The reported ratio correlations−.0560/.5478cannot be reconstructed from printedTable2andTable7using either complete-answer or recruited-group denominators.
study.mechanisms: Adaptation gap, defensive attribution and guilt reduction are proposed interpretations. Expected capability, self-threat, perceived similarity and guilt are not directly measured. Single trustworthiness items are not expectation measures. Source itself recognizes tension in its low-expectation explanation; longer clips are a future conjecture, not a tested repair.
study.scope: No real robot/live collaboration, actual adaptive AI, fault adjudication, behavioral trust, reliance, safety/clinical outcome or tested long-term design benefit. Appearance differences and uncertain labels cannot identify a unique psychological process or justify maximizing user self-blame.

summary: No new record. Enrich existing blame attribution and mind-perception notes; add non-counted construct/interpretation boundaries. Identify mixed agency/experience items and reversed source target descriptions, reporting of critical F values, group-level correlations and unresolved response coding. Preserve approximate support for major descriptive contrasts instead of treating every reporting error as a false result.

findings.definition: Assigning fault or responsibility to an agent for a negative event or outcome.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Users rate self and agent responsibility independently after programmed failure. Avatar groups differ in user self-responsibility, with angel higher than robot in the reported/reconstructable main contrast. Agent-responsibility omnibus does not detect a difference; binary cause-choice omnibusp.0748is nonsignificant.
findings.boundary: Unlike a forced-ratio design, the two ratings need not sum100. Actual fault is not established because failure was scripted regardless of answers. Nonrandomized task recruitment and appearance bundles constrain causal conclusions. Perceived cause/responsibility is not legal liability or justified moral blame.

findings.definition: Ascribing or denying mental capacities to another entity.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: A separate pre-survey rates six target capacities for five avatars. This demonstrates a capacity-attribution procedure, but the published grouping does not cleanly instantiate the cited agency/experience dimensions.
findings.boundary: Preserve broad attribution evidence without treating mixed item averages as validated factors. Scores do not prove actual mental capacities, consciousness, moral status or a uniquely causal mind-perception process. Five means are not319independent observations.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity a capacity for intentional thought, planning and action.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Self-control, memory and morality-related items appear in the pre-survey, but the stated agency score mixes self-control with fear and pleasure. Published construct-specific interpretation needs original administered items and scoring.
findings.boundary: Context only:not reliable new validation of a pure agency score or its superiority/inferiority as a causal predictor. Do not correct by swapping whole labels or infer actual machine agency from appearance.

findings.definition: Attributing to another entity the capacity for subjective feelings or sensations, such as pleasure, pain, fear or joy.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The pre-survey includes fear, pleasure and hunger, but the stated experience score instead combines memory, hunger and morality. Claims that experience matters more rely on five group-level values and this unresolved operationalization.
findings.boundary: Context only:the paper’s composite is not established as the canonical experience measure. No causal effect, individual mediation or actual feeling follows. Preserve source labels as reported with the measurement problem explicit.

findings.definition: The proposal that a discrepancy between expected and experienced agent capabilities shapes the user’s impression of that agent.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: Authors propose that low initial expected dog capability could explain higher post-task trust, and acknowledge that the initial trust ratings do not directly support that story.
findings.boundary: Context only:prior expected capability and perceived performance discrepancy are not measured. Trustworthiness is not the same construct; pre-nonsignificant/post-significant does not establish differential change or resolve the proposed mechanism.

findings.definition: Framing its successes as its own doing and its failures as the fault of the prompt, tools, or user.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The bibliography and responsibility discussion connect the findings to earlier work on self-serving attribution and partner-related defenses.
findings.boundary: Context only:no success-versus-failure contrast or independently known fault establishes a self-serving bias here. Low self-responsibility under an ambiguous programmed failure is not proof of dishonest blame shifting or a motive to protect self-image.

findings.definition: Remorse or self-blame about a perceived moral failure, often accompanied by a wish to repair harm.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The discussion suggests that a robot-like interface might reduce guilt because users assign themselves less responsibility.
findings.boundary: Context only:guilt is not measured. A rating of responsibility is not experienced guilt, and lower guilt is not an established benefit or a reason to manipulate justified accountability.

findings.definition: Inferring a robot’s abilities or functions from its physical form in ways that exceed the available evidence.
findings.novelty_rationale: Retain existing attribution and expectation constructs. A new appearance condition or a problematic operationalization is not a new independent psychological mechanism.
findings.evidence_scope: The paper compares avatar appearances and collects mental-capacity/trust/responsibility ratings. It is relevant context for appearance-based inference, without naming or isolating the FFAB mechanism.
findings.boundary: Context only:one image per identity, nonrandomized recruitment and no validated capability-ground-truth comparison do not establish that every appearance-related inference is an error. Do not relabel a responsibility-group difference as a demonstrated functional-capability bias.

source_corrections.finding: Published item groups mix the cited dimensions. The appropriate intended index grouping is agencyQ2/Q4/Q6andexperienceQ1/Q3/Q5, not first3versuslast3. This is a verified conceptual/table inconsistency, not verified raw-data repair; actual fielded grouping and item responses remain unavailable.

The cited original places God at high agency/low experience and the dog at comparatively low agency/higher experience. The source reverses these descriptions. An angel’s score cannot simply inherit God’s original rating.

2.4004,3.9163and3.9092are the95%critical values for their respective dfs, not observed statistics compatible with the reported pvalues. Rounded-summary reconstruction still supports the main post-trust and self-responsibility contrasts. Document misreporting without silently replacing it with claimed exact raw-data output.

The paragraph describing agencyr−.43/experiencer.39calls the outcome post-trustworthiness. Table6assigns those coefficients to attribution to agent; post-trustworthiness instead has.73/−.59. Correct the outcome label rather than reverse coefficient signs.

No detected initial group difference followed by a detected post-task difference is not a test of differential change. No paired interaction, change-score comparison or baseline-adjusted model is reported. Nonrandom group recruitment adds further uncertainty.

Comparing correlation magnitudes from five avatar means does not demonstrate a causal or statistically tested superiority of experience over agency. Mixed item grouping and unreconciled ratio coefficients further constrain that conclusion.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Table1is visually confirmed as mixing items, but the actual survey form, code and item-level data are unavailable. Do not assert every participant received the wrong form or calculate corrected means from aggregate labels.

Methods describe seven-point Q5responses whileTable7is binary. AngelQ5counts total71versus72recruited; allQ5counts318versus319main participations. Dichotomization, one missing answer and possible withdrawal are not explained.

Using printedTable2andTable7, complete-answer ratios yieldr≈−.00149withagency/.66275withexperience; using recruited denominators yields≈−.00445/.66531. Neither matches−.0560/.5478. Exact underlying ratio/score versions are unverified; do not replace coefficients with purported corrected raw-data values.

Main pairwise pvalues resemble unadjusted two-group tests; the reported Bonferroni implementation is not fully specified. The two main contrasts remain below.05even with10-fold adjustment in rounded-summary checks. Residualp.0866andsymbolsneed original output; categorical omnibus remainsp.0748.

Source asserts little/no relation but supplies no individual-level coefficient/test. Independent rating scales do not themselves prove uncorrelated judgments, and correlations of five means cannot identify individual dependence.

unresolved_source_discrepancies.location: Withdrawal, assignment and prior-study gender argument
unresolved_source_discrepancies.finding: Consent withdrawal is offered after debriefing but counts are absent. Separate online-task recruitment lacks documented random assignment. A different study’s null gender finding does not establish no gender/selection effect in this sample.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: All main significance claims false because Fvalues conflict
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The displayed Fvalues are critical cutoffs. Summary means/SDs/Nsapproximately reproduce the reported major pvalue patterns and significant pairwise contrasts. Retain bounded results rather than reject them wholesale.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: All responsibility judgments forced to sum100
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: Methods explicitly allow independent self/agent0–100ratings. Do not import a zero-sum-slider limitation from another paper.
Printed coefficients reproduce correlations across five condition means from separate pre/main samples. They are not319independent within-person links or causal mediation.

refuted_suspected_errors.location: Guilt, defensive attribution or adaptation gap directly established
refuted_suspected_errors.finding: The study does not measure guilt, self-threat, perceived similarity or expected-versus-observed capability. These are discussion explanations, not isolated tested mechanisms.
Table7reconstructsχ²8.5033, p≈.07479. Approached significance is not a conventional significant result; no actual cause was identified in the scripted-failure task.

methodological_limits: Web convenience recruitment with unequal group demographics and no documented random allocation limits causal claims and generalization beyond these Japanese participants/stimuli.
One avatar per category bundles appearance, identity and style. No universal human-likeness, animal-form, real-robot or cross-cultural design benefit follows.
Failure is experimentally scripted; perceived responsibility and cause are not actual fault, legal liability or evidence that a user should feel guilty.
Published agency/experience composites mix intended items. Scores cannot be repaired without administered materials and item-level records.
Five group-mean correlations, not participant-level mediation, underlie the dimension claims. Greater magnitude does not establish a stronger causal mechanism.
Pre/post trust was measured but no differential-change model is supplied. Trustworthiness is not capability expectation or actual calibrated reliance.
CriticalFvalues are mislabeled, while main pvalue patterns are approximately supported by summaries. Preserve both the error and this counterevidence.

No raw data, analysis code, clinical outcome, physiological index, guilt scale or validated long-term intervention is supplied. No preferred design is recommended to shift justified human accountability.

cross_paper_learning.finding: That paper uses a forced user/robot ratio; this source allows independent ratings. Both require separating perceived responsibility, guilt, cooperation and actual fault, but measurement limitations must not be copied indiscriminately.
Appearance-related attribution and a behavioral correspondence inference differ. Neither automatically establishes a causal attribution error or actual robot disposition.
Both sources use aggregate stimulus scores in some analyses. Five/six group means must not be presented as hundreds of independent individual links, or nulls interpreted as universal equivalence.
Existing Adaptation gap covers the same named hypothesis. This paper supplies an unmeasured explanation rather than a new gap concept or validated mechanism.
Item grouping and factor labels require source-specific checking. Generic mind-perception dimensions do not validate every abbreviated questionnaire or imply actual subjective capacity.

deferred.term: Defensive attribution as a new canonical definition
deferred.reason: The paper first describes attribution of any cause too broadly and later invokes similarity-based protection without directly measuring it. A verified original account distinguishing defensive threat reduction from generic attribution/self-serving bias is needed; the primary source was not fully read here.

deferred.term: Local responsibility as a separate new mechanism
deferred.reason: A broad time/situation-specific responsibility description, not a distinct independently measured behavior in this paper. Existing blame/role/outcome records carry the relevant boundaries.

deferred.term: Adaptation gap as a new row
deferred.reason: Already present. The source does not measure the required expectation/performance discrepancy.

deferred.term: Experience-dominant blame or guilt reduction as new effects
deferred.reason: Unsupported causal interpretation from five means and mixed constructs; guilt is unmeasured. Do not create labels to preserve an overstated finding.

limitations: Zero new records; two existing records receive bounded attribution evidence and six receive non-counted context. Catalogue remains780records in eleven categories. Stable detail IDs, unnumbered rows, seven evaluation criteria and six principles retained. No forced citation quota, invented annual counts, automatic harm edges, full-paper Markdown archive or independent replication claim.
